correctness.rationale: For a fixed root length p, equality of two shortened outputs is equivalent to equality W_t=W_{t+p} at every intervening position, so distinct outputs are exactly maximal match intervals of length at least p. Each interval gives a maximal p-periodic factor of length at least 2p. Fine--Wilf forces its minimum period d to divide p, and maximality then holds also for d, so the factor is a standard run. A run R can receive at most floor(|R|/(2d(R)))=floor(e(R)/2) root labels. Summation proves the structural inequality; the published 2.3n and binary 2.2n run-exponent bounds give the numerical constants. The exhaustive checker independently replays the local correspondence on 4094 binary and 3279 ternary words.

value.rationale: The direct source singles out deg_k^+(n)<=n as an explicit conjecture. The general coefficient 23/20 is within 15 percent of the conjectured coefficient, and the binary coefficient 11/10 is within 10 percent. More importantly, the structural inequality connects square-reduction branching to the well-developed theory of runs, making future run-exponent improvements immediately transferable. This is an infinite structural theorem aimed directly at a published gap, not a routine finite parameter extension.
